prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on your ZIP code, the exact problem, budget, whether you need same‑day service, and whether you prefer a larger company or a local independent. I can, however, help you find the best contractor for your situation and give guidance to pick one you can trust.

Quick questions so I can narrow recommendations:
- What ZIP code or neighborhood in Phoenix?
- Is this an emergency (no cooling at all) or a non‑urgent repair?
- Residential or commercial system? Make/model/age of the AC (if known)?
- Any preference for local business vs national brand?

How to find a great HVAC contractor (checklist)
- License & insurance: Verify the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) license and that they carry general liability and workers’ comp.
- Certifications: Look for NATE‑certified technicians and manufacturer dealer status (Goodman/Trane/Carrier/etc.) if you want brand expertise.
- Reviews & reputation: Check recent Google/Yelp reviews and BBB history (not just star ratings — read recent comments).
- Written estimates: Get at least 2 written estimates that list parts, labor, and warranty.
- Transparent pricing: Ask if they charge by the job (flat rate) or by the hour, and whether diagnostic/service call fee is waived if you hire them.
- Parts & labor warranty: Get the warranty in writing (typical 1–10 years depending on part/manufacturer).
- Emergency service & response time: If it’s hot and your system is down, confirm same‑day or next‑day availability.
- No high‑pressure sales: Watch out for contractors who push immediate full replacement without troubleshooting.

Questions to ask when you call
- Are you licensed and insured in Arizona? What’s your ROC license number?
- Are your technicians NATE‑certified?
- What is your diagnostic fee and is it applied to the repair cost?
- What warranties do you offer on parts and labor?
- Can you give a written estimate before starting work?
- Do you offer emergency/same‑day service?

Where to start (companies commonly available in Phoenix)
- National chains with local Phoenix offices (good if you want brand backing and 24/7 service): One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning, Service Experts, ARS/Rescue Rooter.
- Local independent companies: Phoenix has many well‑reviewed local contractors; independents often offer faster response and lower prices, but verify credentials.

Next step
If you share your ZIP code and whether it’s an emergency, I’ll suggest 3–5 companies near you (national and local) that fit your needs and a recommended script for calling them.
